lines.text: In this world, there's a town where once a year, one family gets to bring a loved one back from the dead.
Huss... huss... huss...
And this year, it was finally my family's turn.
Funny thing is, I can't remember when Mum and Dad died. That part's all fuzzy.
lines.say: Funny thing is, I can't remember when Mum and Dad died. That part's all fuzzy.

lines.text: But my little brother, Leo? I remember it like it was yesterday.
We did everything together. Especially skating.
Kickflips. Grinds. Even the risky stuff Mum banned us from doing.
lines.say: Kickflips. Grinds. Even the risky stuff Mum banned us from doing.

lines.text: Then one day, Leo was skating on the road, and a truck swerved.
I ran faster than I've ever run in my life.
But I was too late.
I haven't been the same since.
So I made up my mind. The wish was his. I was bringing Leo back.
Mum and Dad would understand. They're probably on some trip anyway.
lines.say: Mum and Dad would understand. They're probably on some trip anyway.

lines.text: So I waited. Days went by.
Then, the night before the wish, I saw Icey.
lines.say: Then, the night before the wish, I saw Icy.

lines.text: Icey was our dog. He died a year ago.
lines.say: Icy was our dog. He died a year ago.

lines.text: But there he was. Same floppy ear. Same crooked tail.
And he would not. Stop. Barking.
He kept dragging me toward the cemetery.
No, Icey. I'm not going to look at Leo's grave. He's coming back tomorrow.
lines.say: No, Icy! I'm not going to look at Leo's grave. He's coming back tomorrow.

lines.text: But the barking got louder. And louder.
So I followed him.
We reached the grave, and before I could even read it, I broke down crying.
Then I looked up. And the name on the stone, was mine.
And it all came back.
I wasn't too late. I pushed Leo out of the way. The truck hit me.
Mum and Dad never died. That's why I couldn't remember it.
lines.say: Mum and Dad never died. That's why I couldn't remember it.

lines.text: This isn't the town that brings people back. It's the town they bring people back from.
A ghost town.
But that was okay. Tomorrow was my family's turn. Surely, they'd pick me.
So the day came. I waited by the gate.
Morning. Noon. Midnight.
I was still here.
And Icey, was gone.
They didn't pick me.
They picked the dog.
